output.summary: Turnover rise is real (payroll-reconciled, same counting rules), so the migration-artifact claim fails, and Cedar Hollow's rise (28% to 47%) far exceeds peers (33% to 38%). Causes remain unestablished. Pay is the top exit reason in both years (58% then 61%), so it does not explain the increase, and the market position is unknown. Voluntary exits stepped up in March, before ShiftWise went live, when the Saturday policy took effect firm-wide. No branch-level data exists, and the manager-of-record field is stale at seven branches, so the manager and ShiftWise hypotheses cannot be tested. Vacancy-driven overtime is well supported. Do not approve the irreversible 15% raise or the manager penalties now. Get branch-level data and a pay benchmark before the budget lock, and consider holding the expansion.
